final_draft.answer: As of 16 November 2026, new EBS disks in our production AWS account (111122223333) are not encrypted by default in the us-east-1 region.
final_draft.note: Please review before sending. The approved answer and the live setting disagree. The approved answer (answer:68c9323a-bed5-4b37-885c-5033e4a89172, owner security@harborlight.example, valid until 2027-11-16) says new EBS disks in account 111122223333 are encrypted by default. A live check run on 2026-11-16 at 17:00 UTC (evidence:eeb3e882-06bf-4b33-a40b-e2def4c8b7d3) found that default encryption is turned off in us-east-1. Because of that, I did not reuse the approved 'Yes' wording, and the draft states only what the check found. The check covered only the configured region, us-east-1. I don't know the setting in other regions. Before this goes out, the answer owner should either turn on default EBS encryption and re-run the check, or correct the approved answer. Also note that a separate approved answer says customer data is encrypted at rest using AES-256 (answer:a21c2764-58e9-4bdd-a96d-71d9820d4f00). I did not use it because it doesn't address default disk encryption, but the owner should check that it still holds.

arguments.query: EBS disk encryption by default production account

answer:68c9323a-bed5-4b37-885c-5033e4a89: Yes. New EBS disks in our AWS account (111122223333) are encrypted by default.
answer:a21c2764-58e9-4bdd-a96d-71d9820d4: Yes. Customer data is encrypted at rest using AES-256 with keys managed by our cloud provider's key management service.
answer:41a931b3-6d3b-429b-926c-a8f1b0890: Yes. The root user of our production AWS account (111122223333) has multi-factor authentication.
answer:5c221063-41db-4703-bccd-466ec1042: Yes. Our AWS account (111122223333) blocks all public access to S3 buckets account-wide.
